samuel1.15.p1.b1.text: “The LORD sent me to anoint you king over His people Israel. Now therefore, listen to the words of the LORD.

samuel1.15.p1.b2.text: This is what the LORD of Hosts says: ‘I witnessed what the Amalekites did to the Israelites when they ambushed them on their way up from Egypt.

samuel1.15.p1.b3.text: Now go and attack the Amalekites and devote to destruction all that belongs to them. Do not spare them …

samuel1.15.p2.b1.text: So Saul summoned the troops and numbered them at Telaim—200,000 foot soldiers and 10,000 men of Judah.

samuel1.15.p2.b2.text: Saul came to the city of Amalek and lay in wait in the valley.

samuel1.15.p2.b3.text: “Since you showed kindness to all the Israelites when they came up out of Egypt, go on and get away from the Amalekites …”

samuel1.15.p2.b4.text: So the Kenites moved away from the Amalekites.

samuel1.15.p3.b1.text: Then Saul struck down the Amalekites all the way from Havilah to Shur, which is east of Egypt.

samuel1.15.p3.b2.text: He captured Agag king of Amalek alive …

samuel1.15.p3.b3.text: Saul and his troops spared Agag, along with the best of the sheep and cattle, the fat calves and lambs, and the best of everything else. They were unwilling to destroy them …

samuel1.15.p4.b1.text: “I regret that I have made Saul king, for he has turned away from following Me and has not carried out My instructions.”

samuel1.15.p4.b2.text: And Samuel was distressed and cried out to the LORD all that night.

samuel1.15.p4.b3.text: “Saul has gone to Carmel, and behold, he has set up a monument for himself and has turned and gone down to Gilgal.”

samuel1.15.p5.b1.text: “May the LORD bless you. I have carried out the LORD’s instructions.”

samuel1.15.p5.b2.text: “Then what is this bleating of sheep and lowing of cattle that I hear?”

samuel1.15.p5.b3.text: “The troops brought them from the Amalekites; they spared the best sheep and cattle to sacrifice to the LORD your God …”

samuel1.15.p5.b4.text: “Stop!” exclaimed Samuel. “Let me tell you what the LORD said to me last night.”

samuel1.15.p6.b1.text: “Although you were once small in your own eyes, have you not become the head of the tribes of Israel? The LORD anointed you king over Israel

samuel1.15.p6.b2.text: So why did you not obey the LORD? Why did you rush upon the plunder and do evil in the sight of the LORD?”

samuel1.15.p6.b3.text: “But I did obey the LORD,” Saul replied. “I went on the mission that the LORD gave me. I brought back Agag king of Amalek …

samuel1.15.p6.b4.text: The troops took sheep and cattle from the plunder, the best of the things devoted to destruction, in order to sacrifice them to the LORD your God at Gilgal.”

samuel1.15.p7.b1.text: “Does the LORD delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices as much as in obedience to His voice? Behold, obedience is better than sacrifice, and attentiveness is better than the fat of rams.

samuel1.15.p7.b2.text: For rebellion is like the sin of divination, and arrogance is like the wickedness of idolatry.

samuel1.15.p7.b3.text: Because you have rejected the word of the LORD, He has rejected you as king.”

samuel1.15.p8.b1.text: “I have sinned; I have transgressed the LORD’s commandment and your instructions, because I feared the people and obeyed their voice. Now therefore, please forgive my sin and return with me so I can worship the LORD.”

samuel1.15.p8.b2.text: “I will not return with you,” Samuel replied. “For you have rejected the word of the LORD, and He has rejected you as king over Israel.”

samuel1.15.p8.b3.text: “The LORD has torn the kingdom of Israel from you today and has given it to your neighbor who is better than you.

samuel1.15.p8.b4.text: Moreover, the Glory of Israel does not lie or change His mind …

samuel1.15.p9.b1.text: “I have sinned,” Saul replied. “Please honor me now before the elders of my people and before Israel. Come back with me …”

samuel1.15.p9.b2.text: So Samuel went back with Saul, and Saul worshiped the LORD.

samuel1.15.p9.b3.text: “Surely the bitterness of death is past.”

samuel1.15.p9.b4.text: “As your sword has made women childless, so your mother will be childless among women.”

samuel1.15.p10.b1.text: Then Samuel went to Ramah, but Saul went up to his home in Gibeah of Saul.

samuel1.15.p10.b2.text: And to the day of his death, Samuel never again visited Saul. Samuel mourned for Saul,

samuel1.15.p10.b3.text: and the LORD regretted that He had made Saul king over Israel.
